source_text:
21 Τοὺς τῶν ψεκτῶν προσώπων λόγους οὐκ ἀλληγορήσεις, οὐδὲ ζητήσεις τι
πνευματικὸν ἐν αὐτοῖς, πλὴν εἰ μὴ δι' οἰκονομίαν ὁ Θεὸς ἐνήργησεν, ὡς ἐν τῷ
Βαλαὰμ καὶ Καϊάφᾳ, ἵνα ὁ μὲν περὶ γενέσεως, ὁ δὲ περὶ θανάτου τοῦ Σωτῆρος ἡμῶν
προείπῃ.
22 ∆εῖ δὲ μὴ σκυθρωπὸν εἶναι τὸν γνωστικὸν μηδὲ δυσπρόσιτον· τὸ μὲν γὰρ
ἀγνοοῦντός ἐστι τοὺς λόγους τῶν γινομένων· τὸ δὲ μὴ βουλομένου πάντας
ἀνθρώπους σωθῆναι καὶ εἰς ἐπίγνωσιν ἀληθείας ἐλθεῖν.
24 Πρόσεχε σεαυτῷ μήποτε κέρδους ἕνεκεν ἢ τοῦ εὐπαθεῖν, ἢ δόξης χάριν
παρερχομένης, εἴπῃς τι τῶν ἀπορρήτων καὶ βληθῇς ἔξω τῶν ἱερῶν περιβόλων, ὡς
καὶ αὐτὸς ἐν τῷ ναῷ τὰ τῆς περιστερᾶς τέκνα πιπράσκων.
27 Μὴ ἀπερισκέπτως θεολογήσῃς, μηδέποτε ὁρίζου τὸ θεῖον· τῶν γὰρ
γεγονότων καὶ συνθέτων εἰσὶν οἱ ὅροι.
28 .............................................. ........ ὅτι μισεῖ κακίαν ὁ πειραθεὶς κακίαν, πεῖρα
δὲ τῆς ἐγκαταλείψεως ἔγγονος .............................
29 Οἱ διδασκόμενοι λεγέτωσάν σοι ἀεὶ τό· φίλε προσανάβηθι ἄνω· αἰσχρὸν
γάρ ἐστιν ἀναβάντα σε πάλιν ὑπὸ τῶν ἀκουόντων κατενεχθῆναι.
30 Φιλάργυρός ἐστιν οὐχ ὁ ἔχων χρήματα, ἀλλ' ὁ ἐφιέμενος τούτων· τὸν γὰρ
οἰκονόμον εἶναί φασι βαλάντιον λογικόν.
1
31 Γέροντας μὲν θυμοῦ, τοὺς δὲ νέους γαστρὸς κρατεῖν παρακάλει· τοὺς μὲν
γὰρ οἱ ψυχικοί, τοὺς δὲ ἐπὶ πλεῖστον οἱ σωματικοὶ διαμάχονται δαίμονες.
32 Ἔμφραττε στόματα τῶν καταλαλούντων ἐν ἀκοαῖς σου· καὶ μὴ θαυμάσῃς
ὑπὸ πλείστων κατηγορούμενος· οὗτος γὰρ ὁ πειρασμὸς ἐκ δαιμόνων· τὸν γὰρ
γνωστικὸν ἐλεύθερον εἶναι δεῖ μίσους καὶ μνησικακίας, καὶ μὴ βουλομένων.
33 Λέληθεν ἴσως ἑαυτὸν θεραπεύων ὁ διὰ τὸν Κύριον τοὺς ἀνθρώπους
ἰώμενος· ὃ γὰρ προσάγει φάρμακον ὁ γνωστικός, τὸν μὲν πλησίον ἐνδεχομένως,
ἑαυτὸν δὲ ἀναγκαίως ἰᾶται.
thought_title: Not allegorizing the bad, guarding speech and temper
orientation: Evagrius continues his counsels to the gnostic on when not to speak of divine things and how to remain free from anger and accusation.
pass_a_gloss: 21 You will not allegorize the words of blameworthy persons, nor will you seek anything spiritual in them, except if God worked through divine arrangement, as in Balaam and Caiaphas, in order that the one might foretell concerning the birth and the other concerning the death of our Savior. 22 The gnostic must not be gloomy nor hard to approach; for the first is of one who is ignorant of the principles of the things that come to be; and the second is of one who does not wish all men to be saved and to come to recognition of truth. 24 Take heed to yourself lest for the sake of gain or for the sake of enjoying comfort, or for the sake of passing glory, you say something of the secret teachings and you be thrown outside the holy enclosures, as also the one selling in the temple the young of the dove. 27 Do not speak about God without examination, and never define the divine; for definitions belong to made and composite things. 28 [large lacuna] that the one who has been tried hates evil, and trial is offspring of abandonment [lacuna]. 29 Let those who are being taught always say to you: friend come up higher; for it is shameful that after you have gone up you be brought down again by those who hear. 30 The lover of money is not the one who has money, but the one who desires these things; for they say the steward is a rational purse. 31 Exhort old men to master anger, and the young to master the belly; for ensouled demons fight the former, and bodily demons for the most part fight the latter. 32 Plug the mouths of those who speak ill in your hearing; and do not be amazed while being accused by very many; for this trial is from demons; for the gnostic must be free from hatred and from holding memory of injury, and from those who are unwilling. 33 Perhaps he has escaped his own notice while healing himself, the one who through the Lord heals men; for what drug the gnostic brings forward, he heals his neighbor possibly, but himself necessarily.

bible_refs.note: πάντας ἀνθρώπους σωθῆναι καὶ εἰς ἐπίγνωσιν ἀληθείας ἐλθεῖν

pass_b_english: Do not allegorize the words of blameworthy people, and do not look for anything spiritual in them, unless God through divine arrangement has worked in them, as with Balaam and Caiaphas, so that the one foretold our Savior's birth and the other foretold His death.

The gnostic must be neither gloomy nor hard to approach. Gloom belongs to one who does not know the principles of the things that come to be, and being hard to approach belongs to one who does not want all people to be saved and to come to recognition of the truth (1 Timothy 2:4).

Watch yourself, lest for the sake of gain or comfort, or for the sake of passing glory, you speak anything of the secret teachings and are cast outside the sacred enclosures, like a man selling the young of doves in the temple.
Do not speak about God recklessly, and never define the divine. Definitions belong to things that have been made and put together.
[Part of the text is missing.] The one who has been tried by evil hates evil, and trial is the child of abandonment. [Part of the text is missing.]
Let those you teach always say to you, "Friend, come up higher" (Luke 14:10). For it is shameful, after you have gone up, to be pulled down again by your hearers.
The lover of money is not the one who has money, but the one who longs for it. For they say the steward is a reasoning purse.
Urge older men to master anger and younger men to master the belly. For demons that war against the soul assail the former, while demons that war against the body for the most part assail the latter.

Shut the mouths of those who speak ill of others within your hearing, and do not be surprised when many accuse you. That trial comes from demons. For the gnostic must be free from hatred and from holding memory of injury, even when others do not wish it.
The one who heals people for the sake of the Lord may heal himself without noticing it. For the remedy the gnostic offers heals his neighbor possibly, but heals himself necessarily.
notes: Section 28 is damaged with long lacunae before and after the preserved clause; gloss marks gaps and does not restore missing text.
Stray 1 after section 30 is not translated as source text.
Section 32 ending καὶ μὴ βουλομένων is elliptical; glossed literally as and from those who are unwilling without supplying an object.

last_rejected.quote: demons that war against the soul assail the former, while demons that war against the body for the most part assail the latter
last_rejected.source_quote: τοὺς μὲν γὰρ οἱ ψυχικοί, τοὺς δὲ ἐπὶ πλεῖστον οἱ σωματικοὶ διαμάχονται δαίμονες
last_rejected.why: ψυχικοί/σωματικοί classify the demons; they fight the elders and youths, not soul and body as targets.
last_rejected.fix: Urge older men to master anger and younger men to master the belly. Psychic demons war chiefly against the former, bodily demons mostly against the latter.
last_rejected.ruling: In Evagrian usage, ψυχικοί and σωματικοί denote demons targeting soul/body passions, and τοὺς μέν/δέ ('former/latter') still receive διαμάχονται ('assail').

last_rejected.quote: free from hatred and from holding memory of injury, even when others do not wish it
last_rejected.source_quote: ἐλεύθερον εἶναι δεῖ μίσους καὶ μνησικακίας, καὶ μὴ βουλομένων
last_rejected.why: μὴ βουλομένων is a third genitive parallel to hatred and resentment, not a clause about others’ wishes.
last_rejected.fix: For the gnostic must be free from hatred, from holding a grudge, and from ill will.
last_rejected.ruling: καὶ μὴ βουλομένων is a concessive genitive absolute ('even against their will'), not a third genitive parallel to μίσους καὶ μνησικακίας.
